utterances.text: And just for completeness, if we go to the last page just to confirm that it's signed by the minister since I don't have the hard copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do that, can you also confirm that it contains the same reference as the previous one that you looked at with me to the chiefs of the SUPs and the RDB centres and departments in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's written in the decision, in one of the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in your role as chief for communications under this order, under this decision, from June 1st, 1999, onwards, did you have any official contact with RDB personnel who were said to be members of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During that brief period I worked on the staff from the 1st of June, I did not have any contact with members of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The other question I have was also related to a question by Judge Bonomy at page 38, lines 14 through 17, when you were talking about the temporary switchboard, the temporary telephone exchange that was set up within Serbia itself and you said but not in Kosovo. And then in these lines you said at 15th or 17: "After June 1999 when I came there this telephone exchange was operational. I don't know when it was installed, this temporary solution with this smaller capacity telephone exchange and switchboard." When you came in June 1999, where, sir, is this talking about -- where did you come to with respect to this answer? Where was the temporary telephone exchange operational?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Belgrade, and that temporary switchboard was used for mutual communication between MUP members in the city of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I believe in questioning by my colleague Mr. Hannis you were talking about the hand-held radios, the ultra-high frequency and very high-frequency, UHF, VHF. Were these used by all police and not just PJP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the range allocated to the ministry, according to the plan of distribution. All units of the ministry in the territory of Serbia used that range.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the last matter I'd like to clear up -- strike that. Two matters I need to clear up. First, with respect to the document that Mr. Cepic showed you, the military document talking about the operation of the radio station Free Kosovo during the course of the war, could you verify for me -- I can't recall if you -- if the specific instance that you had was prior to the commencement of bombings, the specific contact that you had with members of the ministry of telecommunications? Was that before or after the commencement of bombings by NATO forces?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before the beginning of air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now the last area I'd like to clear up with you, I believe, relates to confusion that might have been caused by my awkward wording of the questions relating to the designations of the MUP units in P1052, if we could for the moment have P1052 up on the screen again, just around the same page. If we look at -- oops, 1052, P1052. If we could look at this first page now for the moment, sir. We see there in the third line it says the 3rd OD, which would be the Serbian odred, MUP as I think you said. Was there, in fact, any MUP or PJP detachment that had the permanent name as the 3rd odred or 3rd Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my prior testimony, that's exactly what I said, that detachments did not have a one-digit number before them. It couldn't be 3rd, 5th, or 6, they were 35th, 37th, and I don't know any more, but it was always a two-digit or three-digit number in the name of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say that there was always a two-digit or three-digit number in the name of the detachment, would that designation be permanent, whereas the radio call-sign could be changed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the interpretation. Could the interpreters repeat this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll help out. I'll read back my question. And when you say that there was always a two-digit or a three-digit number in the name of the detachment, would that name designation be permanent, whereas the radio call-sign could be changed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the name of the detachment was permanent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Hannis showed you a military document from the time-period showing certain named designations for PJP units of only one number. I'd like to show you a police document, P1993, which I believe Mr. Hannis had on his list if -- I don't recall if he utilised it, he might have even utilised it. And I think on the first page we'll see -- looking down, sir, at items number 5 through 14 on the list of persons who were present, are these the proper designations for the PJP units that you were familiar with that would have been on the terrain in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have an objection to the form of that question. The object I showed him, Exhibit P1434, was from September of 1998. I think we need to distinguish that this is May 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, Mr. Hannis asked the witness to draw speculations and conclusions of what is possible from a military document. I think looking at a police document we have a much clearer picture from a police witness, especially given his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, you showed him this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, and it's dated the 11th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct, but the one I showed him to ask him if there were PJP detachments with single digits was P1434 from September 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but it's open to counsel to point to other material which might have a bearing on the accuracy of the document that you were looking at, Mr. Hannis. We will repel that objection and allow you to proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Deretic, my question was, directing your attention to lines -- pardon me, to items that are numbered 5 through 14 of participants, and the question I had for you was: Do those two- and three-digit name designations for PJP units -- I'm sorry, it goes all the way actually through the 17, I didn't have the whole document on the screen. Those are all two- or three-digit name designations for what PJP units? Are those the ones you're familiar with, I guess I should say?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. Those are the real designations, the real names of PJP detachments, as they did in these items you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in the course of your duties in 1998, had these name designations for the PJP been any different according to the MUP regulations would you have expected to be made aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DERETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These detachment names, as they are stated here in this document, were there throughout the presence of those detachments in the area of Kosovo and Metohija. I'm not aware of anything changing there. The same names were used in the course of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just waiting for the transcript and translation. Thank you, Mr. Deretic, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Deretic, that completes your evidence here. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give evidence. You may now leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Our next witness is Mr. Gavranic, Dusan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gavranic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You'll now be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Gavranic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to break the ice, can you please try to introduce yourself to us briefly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: My name is Dusan Gavranic. I was born on the 25th of December, 1951. My father's name is Bozo and my mother's name is Ljubica. I am married my wife's name is called Verica, I have three children, Slobodan, Dusko, and Nemanja. I completed my elementary school in "Banacki Despotovac," that's where I was born. I completed high school in Zrenjanin and the faculty of philosophy in Belgrade. Upon completion of my studies, for a while I played soccer professionally from 1975 until 1978 in Proleter Zrenjanin club which was a first-league club at the time. I began to work as a professor in 1978 in the secondary traffic and agricultural school in Zrenjanin. I worked there as a professor and also a director until 1989. From 1989 until 1992, I was vice-president of the municipality or Municipal Assembly of Zrenjanin. On the 1st of April, 1992, I was appointed chief of the Zrenjanin SUP, the secretariat for internal affairs in Zrenjanin. On the 1st of January, 1999, I was sent to Kosovo to perform the duties of the chief of the secretariat of internal affairs in Gnjilane from my post as chief of the SUP in Zrenjanin. The chief of the Gnjilane SUP -- I was the chief until July 1999, when I returned to Zrenjanin, again as chief of the Zrenjanin SUP. I was at that post until the 20th of March, 2001, and then I was appointed as the responsible person for the department of driving tests and I carried out those duties until the 21st of December, 2004, which was when I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to ask you: Who appointed you to all the posts that you were appointed to in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: All the duties I was appointed to by the minister or by the decision of the chief of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're going to tell us now about the organizational structure of the Gnjilane SUP, first of all, territorially and then structurally?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The secretariat for internal affairs in Gnjilane encompassed the territories of four municipalities, Gnjilane, Vitina, Kosovska Kamenica, and Novo Brdo. The secretariat seat was in Gnjilane, it had two departments of internal affairs, Kosovska Kamenica and Kosovska Vitina as well as a police station in Novo Brdo as part of its organization. That is how it looked in the organizational sense; in the functional sense, the secretariat comprised sections and departments. The Gnjilane SUP had criminal police, police departments, traffic police departments, and also common affairs department. The sections were section -- the section for communications, border police, automatic data processing, I can't remember if there were any other sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a fire-fighting police sector?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, the fire-fighting sector was there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the difference between a section or sector and a department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Odelenje" is a broader term. It's a department, it could also have sectors as part of it; but there were also independent sectors which were not part of a department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that as part of the Gnjilane SUP you had two OUPs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who were the chiefs, the number 1 persons, of these internal affairs departments?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The Kosovska Kamenica internal affair department had Momcilo Trajkovic as its chief; the Vitina OUP had Sefkija Hamza as its chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sefkija Hamza, what ethnicity was he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the members of your SUP, did they include personnel of Albanian ethnicity other than the chief of the internal affairs department?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were not a large number but there were both at the seat of the secretariat and also in the internal affairs department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And were there any members of the state security sector in your department?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, these are two different departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you cooperate with the state security sector chief and did you know which organizational unit of this department existed in Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It was part of the State Security Service of Gnjilane and Urosevac. The cooperation was such that it mainly comprised exchange of data about security incidents and other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something briefly about the PJP and then I'll go back to this question. Was there an independent PJP company in the Gnjilane SUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the Gnjilane SUP territory, did it have any PJP company that was sent to Kosovo and Metohija from Serbia proper?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, there were no such companies sent from Serbia proper to the secretariat territory. No, there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about detachments?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, no detachments either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this now that had to do with the duty service. Did your SUP at its seat have a duty service?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did have a duty service at its seat, also the internal affairs departments in Vitina and Kosovska Kamenica had duty services as well, as well as the police station in Novo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in any period after you came - and you arrived on the 1st of January, 1999 - what were these duty operations services relocated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the war broke out and after the bombing, the duty services were relocated, and they practically functioned in completely new circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what these new circumstances were, how did they function after relocation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: After the relocation, especially after the bombing of the Pristina building when all the communications were severed, the duty service was functioning with extreme difficulty, practically there were no telephone or teleprinter or dispatch communications. So from that period onward, and practically throughout the whole period of the war, the duty service functioned via messenger or courier, so courier communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what did one shift of the duty service in the SUP seat have as staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: You had the communication chief, his assistant, also the police officer at the reception, police officer who was securing the building, and also two reinforced patrols all operated as one duty shift. So it was about 12 people, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the term, the man who was at the head of all of that, can you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Chief or head or shift leader of the duty service, shift leader of the duty service and the others were police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the duty service in the internal affairs departments and police stations, was it organized in an identical way as in the SUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was organized in exactly the same way, both in the Kosovska Kamenica and Vitina SUP departments, as well as at the Novo Brdo police station; but the personnel was -- there were fewer personnel in the shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain how the seat of the MUP in Belgrade was reported to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The reporting to the Belgrade seat was conducted via the duty service, so the duty service of the SUP would pass on information to the duty operations centre of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia in Belgrade. This information was received from the SUP departments and the police station duty services.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Along with reporting to the Belgrade staff, did you also inform the staff in Pristina about these events?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The security occurrences and information were passed on both to the Belgrade MUP seat and also to the Pristina MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have to also report to civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes. When urgent information was required as one of the basic types of reporting, then the information that had to do with the secretariat, all the municipal and local authorities were informed, the chief of the district, et cetera, as well as the Pristina and Belgrade staffs, the same information was passed to all of them, especially if it was something urgent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was the information that you sent to the head of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The president of the municipality or the chief of the district was informed, for example, about large fires, maintenance breakdowns, serious traffic accidents with casualties, obstacles, barriers, or roadblocks. This is something that is part of the rule books on information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you pass on any information about the bombing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, the bombing too. We reported to the municipal organs and the district organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because this rule on information is not translated, I am not able to show it to you. So we will just proceed without it. So according to the rules on information or reporting, what were the forms of reporting that the SUP had to carry out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Three main forms: Urgent informing, daily reports, and interim reports. Then you had urgent, daily, or periodic reports, which could be monthly or annual reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you stick to these rules?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, all the secretariats abided by these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to understand the term "izvestavanje," reporting, in the MUP we also need to understand the organization. So can we please look at P1044 on the e-court, please. Can you please tell us this first. What is the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The document bears the date 19th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that at the time there was a change in the name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The change was from milicija to policija, militia to police?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was an organizational change. The term "policija" was replaced with the -- the term milicija was replaced with the term policija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who sent this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This document was sent by the public security sector of the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us to whom the document was sent?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The document was sent to the secretariat for internal affairs, all organizational units at the seat of the ministry, to all organizational units which are not part of the department, to all the ministry staffs in Pristina and Prijepolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that it was being sent separately to the MUP staff, and there were two at the time, one in Pristina and one in Prijepolje. Does the staff belong to any group of the bodies cited in the first three lines of the document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, you can see that from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at the first paragraph under I?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: "According to the rules of the internal organization of the Ministry of the Interior adopted on the 5th of April, 1996, the following organizational changes have been made ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what is the document that we see in front of us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This is a document informing us which administrations, which secretariats existed as organizational units, and it's provided for our information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it has to do with organizational changes and not just the change of names?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, first of all it deals with organizational changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is stated under Roman I, Arabic 1?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The following organizational units have been established at the ministry head office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have to read them all.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: And then we have the administration and the organizational centres that were created.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 states: "For carrying out tasks within the competence of the ministry, i.e., public security tasks, secretariats of the interior for municipalities have been established according to local jurisdiction, with main offices in ..." and then the offices are listed and they go to number 33. So there were 33 secretariats in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what sort of units are secretariats?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Organizational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do they cover?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The territory of municipalities, several municipalities, two or more municipalities, depending on the size of the towns that they're in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about 1999, was there the same number of secretariats?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now on the next page, page 2 under number 3, what is stated there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The following organizational units have been established outside the structure of the department: 1. College of internal affairs in Zemun;. 2. Secondary school of internal affairs in Sremska Kamenica. 3. Institute for security. 4. Department for systemic and legal affairs."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at Roman II and then paragraph 1 in that section, what is that about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Roman II, number 1 says: "Departments of the interior and/or police stations shall report all occurrences, developments and information of interest to security to the secretariat of interior of which it is a part (from here on: The secretariat) and the secretariat shall inform the ministry. "Direct communication with the ministry or another secretariat shall be established in extremely urgent situations and for message in importance to security."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you something in relation to that. In practice were reports written every day, regardless of whether something happened or not or were reports truly sent only about occurrences that were of security-related interest?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Reports were sent on occurrences that were of interest to security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If there were no such occurrences?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: There were no reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please look at page 3. We need item 4. Does this paragraph show who the police stations in charge of border crossing control sent information to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It reads as follows: "The stations in charge of border crossing control send information directly to the authorised department in the ministry and the secretariat on whose territory they are located," that is to say that they have a direct functional link to the ministry, and they also send these reports to the secretariat on whose territory they are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does paragraph 5 tell us now, is it characteristic only of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 says that: "Secretariats of the interior in Pristina, Kosovska Mitrovica, Urosevac, Gnjilane, Djakovica, Pec, and Prizren send dispatches both to the ministry and the ministry staff in Pristina" at the same time. It says practically that these dispatches are sent along parallel lines with the dispatches that are sent to the duty operations centre in Belgrade, that they are also CC'd to the staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that what actually happened in practice? Did you send these parallel reports?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have Roman III, and it pertains to communication by way of dispatches. Could you please look at page 4 now and paragraph 5 on that page. What kind of reporting is this about.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 says: "When an organizational unit from the ministry main office sends dispatches, it addresses them as follows: 1. SUP - to all (1-33) staff of the ministry - Pristina. 2 SUP in (the name of secretariat). 3. Border control police station to all and KPDG (plus the name of the police station) number 1 is stated down here. It says staff of the Ministry/Pristina but there is no number there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the staff was an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the staff was not an organizational unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What exactly is meant by that, Mr. Lukic, on organizational unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what I asked him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 4 it talks about communication between organizational units being conducted in the manner set out in this circular, which would suggest that everything in paragraph 5 is an organizational unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have four numbers here, and it's obvious that MUP staff was informed only at the same time when SUPs are informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we will be dealing with that, with organizational structure of MUP, and it would be clear that MUP staff is -- was not an organizational unit inside the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What does that mean, though, being an organizational unit? It's a concept in the English language I don't really follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I could clarify it with this witness as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be a language problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, what is an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior? Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior were territorial and functional organizational units primarily; that is to say the territory of the Republic of Serbia is divided into secretariats that are territorial organizational units. And from a functional point of view, the territory of the Republic of Serbia is divided into administrations, every one of them covers the entire territory of Serbia for their particular line of work. For example, the crime police administration in Belgrade covers problems related to the crime police and their departments at the level of all of Serbia, if that was of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that the rules on reporting have not been translated. It is 6D1323, that's how it's been marked in this case, and in article 1 it refers to types of reporting. What kind of types of reporting exist, Mr. Gavranic, within the MUP of Serbia? Can you repeat that for us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Within the MUP of Serbia there are --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Urgent, daily, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, my colleague has an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I just raise an objection to the use of this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not using the document; I just said so. I'm not using the document. I don't need it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Counsel's using a document in examination-in-chief which, according to the orders of the Court, as I understand the issue he should have notified us about in his notification filed last week, which he did not. In addition to that, the document had not been translated. I raise the objection primarily because as far as this witness is concerned the majority of the documents that we have been notified about we were notified over the weekend, mostly sometime last night. We have not made objections when we have been notified quite late with some of the documents or the document, but when the majority of the documents are not notified to us in accordance with the Court order, it indicates that the Defence is treating the Court order as meaningless; and therefore, I raise this objection in addition to the obvious frustration and difficulties that it puts the Prosecution under.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think I would prefer to deal with that point in the context of a particular document, and I'd be grateful if you would raise it when that occurs, when a document that was notified late is referred to. But here Mr. Lukic unwisely has twice now told us he's not using a document because it's not been translated, and is then asking the witness questions that could be interpreted as being questions about the document. However, so far it looks as though the witness has been able to answer these questions from his own personal knowledge and without particular reference to the document. It is not an entirely satisfactory situation, Mr. Lukic, but please proceed with the questions on this particular issue. We'll deal with the broader issue as and when it arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Especially unsatisfactory for us, Your Honours, because we have to deal with the witnesses without the documents. We would rather have them in front of our witness, but because the court service was not able to translate it in a timely manner --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I deliberately avoided getting involved in the issue over responsibility for this, bearing in mind you've had something like - what is now? - approaching three years to prepare your case. Let's not go down that road. Let's work with what we've got and do our best to get through it. And if you particularly want to use untranslated documents, then you should make an application to us and identify the particular circumstances that have arisen to result in you not having the document translated at this late stage and we'll look at it on its merits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just pointing the paragraphs for our use later on because we could find the references in this document when it's translated. So I'm not showing this document to the witness, and when I said "paragraph 1" of this document, it just means that we would be able to check later on when it's translated what's really in that document. That's my only point I wanted to draw. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since my colleague Mr. Stamp objected at that moment, we'll go back to what I asked you then. What types of reporting is listed, and you said urgent and daily and what else was there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Urgent, daily, and periodical reporting, those are the types.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Articles 7 through 10 of the instructions, urgent reporting was dealt with, and I'm going to ask you what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Urgent reporting for the territory of a SUP pertains to all occurrences related to different fields of security. For instance, as far as crime is concerned, and it's killings, theft, robbery, and so on; then any kind of breakdown in law and order, traffic accidents resulting in fatalities, traffic accidents involving several persons, foreign nationals, then fires, explosions; I've already said roadblocks, strikes, the stay and movement of foreigners; falsifications of different documents, such as passports and IDs, and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did urgent reporting take place up until the bombing and how did it take place after the bombing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Urgent reporting primarily took place via telephone dispatches and radio. After the bombing all of this practically became non-existent, I'm talking about my secretariat where I was chief. So after the bombing when the lines were down, urgent reporting primarily took place by way of couriers, courier mail to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have on e-court 6D852, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You do have this document in your binder, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of a document is this in terms of page 1?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This shows that this document was sent by the Vitina police station. It is addressed to the SUP in Gnjilane, the police department in Gnjilane. It was signed by the commander of the police station. Further on one can -- may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 3 of this document now.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was reporting to who over here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The SUP in Gnjilane is reporting to the Ministry of the Interior, namely, the crime police administration and along parallel lines the staff for the ministry of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina. This has to do with urgent reporting pertaining to the crime of homicide.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it the same occurrence regarding which you received information in Gnjilane, as you explained while looking at the previous documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same thing. It is a killing in the village of Kabas, Shefqet Mustafa was killed. And according to this information, I mean this official note speaks of how this killing took place and what information was available. This information was provided by Svetozar Peric, chief, to the Belgrade MUP and the staff for Kosovo in Pristina. So that is this functional way of reporting because the report is sent to the crime police administration of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If it was a military conscript who had committed this crime, what would you do then?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at this dispatch, page 3, in addition to the description of the way it occurred, it is said that the usual procedure was followed, the judge on duty, Drago Stoiljkovic, came on site. It says the perpetrator is a military conscript, and therefore the military police of the Army of Yugoslavia was informed and would proceed and take appropriate measures against the said member of the VJ according to regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have good cooperation with military bodies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they assist you in the follow-up when their members were concerned?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I can speak only in my own name. We had good cooperation when suspects, perpetrators, were members of the military and a good number of these cases were elucidated and prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the usual procedure when the first report of a crime comes in to the duty service?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: When a duty service receives a report that a crime is committed -- has been committed, let's say the most serious crime, murder, it sends a patrol to secure the site. If there is no patrol available in the vicinity of the site, then the duty service urgently sends a patrol from the duty service itself. That patrol goes to the site to secure the site and to meet the patrol that normally works in that sector. At the same time, an urgent report is sent to the investigating judge on duty, and he comes with his entire team; and from the moment of his arrival it is the investigating judge who takes over the entire procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the next type of reporting after urgent?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It is daily reporting. A daily bulletin of incidents is made up in the duty service listing all the incidents and events for the past 24 hours. Up to 400 hours, that is 4.00 a.m., the duty service must send that bulletin to the duty operations centre in Belgrade, which receives such bulletins from 33 different secretariats. And on the basis of all these 33 it proceeds to draft the daily bulletin of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. Can I just go back slightly on this. You said that the perpetrator of that killing was a VJ military conscript --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you -- you would have nothing more to do with the matter; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the moment when the investigating judge comes to the scene, he leads all further investigation, he organizes the crime police from the SUP of Gnjilane to assist him, and the whole procedure ends with the filing of a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the police is concerned, that is, the procedure ends with a filing of a criminal report. And if I may add, that criminal report may later be qualified differently by the prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Filed where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the prosecution office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which prosecution office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Municipal or district. Since this is a homicide, it would be in the district prosecutor's office in the town of Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's puzzling me is one of your answers is partially translated as follows, it says the perpetrator is a military conscript, and therefore the military police of the VJ was informed and would proceed and take appropriate members -- measures against the said member of the VJ. And what I'm trying to sort out in my mind is whether this particular event was dealt with through the ordinary civil process or whether it was dealt with by military justice. Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to explain. At the moment when this incident occurred, nobody knew it was a military conscript. When it was found out from operative sources that it was a military conscript, the investigating judge has already done his work. The criminal report was filed by the SUP to the prosecutor's office. What happens later, whether the case was given to the military prosecutor, the police doesn't know. And as to why we informed the military police, that's because they have their own different procedures, such as disciplinary proceedings. I don't want to go into the regulations governing the Army of Yugoslavia, but I believe that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The reason I'm going back over this with you is that in quite a number of examples that we see of crimes being committed, my impression is that there is loads of room for the investigation to fall between two stools; and here was one I thought we might nail, but no such luck. So let's proceed. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We stopped at daily reporting and that you had to file your daily report by 4.00 a.m. the next morning to the base of the ministry in Belgrade. I'd like to ask you, after the beginning of air-strikes, was it always possible to file this daily report on time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, it was not because the system of communications was broken down, was disrupted, the daily report was sent by courier depending on the situation that day, sometimes the bulletin would be several days late.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did the duty operations centre of the ministry do with the bulletins they received from you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I think I've already said this, but I'll repeat. The duty operations centre, once it receives daily bulletins from 33 secretariats, proceeds to write a daily bulletin covering all of Serbia with all its security-related events and incidents; and to whom this bulletin is sent, that is something the chief of secretariat decides.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We said there was urgent and daily reporting. What is the third type?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Periodical reporting, that would be monthly and annual. The analytics department, once it had received all daily bulletins, prepares a monthly bulletin and the same happens once a year, an annual analysis is made, and again the chief of sector decides to whom this is sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did secretariats of internal affairs from Kosovo and Metohija have the obligation to send their periodical reports to the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The periodical ones, no, only urgent and daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In practice did you send those periodical reports to the staff? We know now that you didn't have, but did you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember whether the periodical report was sent to them in practice. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After the air-strikes began, you said it was technically no longer possible to send reports the normal way. You sent them by messenger, by courier, that's from your end; but did you have problems receiving reports from lower organizational units?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It was absolutely the same. When we were receiving reports from Vitina, Kosovska Kamenica, or elsewhere, again we had to use courier service and bulletins would come in late depending on the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the territory of your secretariat, do you remember when the telephone and telegraph traffic stopped?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: In the night of the 28th of March, the SUP Pristina was hit and all telephone and telegraph lines were destroyed, several days later the post office was bombed, and that was the moment when we in our secretariat shifted to courier service. It was a very dangerous situation and fear from air-strikes was great. At one point we in the police even threw away our cell phones because they were emitting signals of mobile telephony and that could be used for locating.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now something about work-plans. Who made the general work-plan for all organizational units in the entire territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The general work-plan was made by the Ministry of the Interior, for the territory of the whole republic it would make a general work-plan, and then organizational units would work according to that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know which document governs this procedure?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: That is stipulated in the rules of internal organization of the MUP, and this work-plan is binding the secretariats to make their own work-plans. They have to do this according to the format prescribed by particular administrations, such as the crime police administration. They get a list of points that have to be covered and every department of crime police has to follow the format prescribed by the general crime police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the work-plans are made according to prescribed lines?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Lower-level work-plans are made for separate lines of work, and if the administration in charge verifies, let's say, the work-plan made by the Gnjilane department then Gnjilane was free to follow their work-plan. If there were any corrections to be made, the draft work-plan would be returned to the department and revised and then sent again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll continue on this topic, but now we have to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, we have to break now for lunch, that will be for an hour. Could you please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we will see you again at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavranic, we were talking about plans, according to which organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior worked. Could you please tell us what organ verifies the work-plans of the organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Verification is carried out by the administrations in charge, that is to say the administration of the crime police, they verify the plan of the crime police department in Gnjilane and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the role of the secretariat of the interior in that process?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The secretariat of the interior brings together these individual plans of work, and it makes its own plan of work on the basis of priorities that had been set by the administrations that are in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were in Kosovo and Metohija, did the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija adopt a plan or plans according to which organizational units of the ministry worked?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, it didn't in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the work-plans, did you send them to the MUP staff for verification?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No. The work-plans were sent for verification to the headquarters of the responsible administrations in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were reports being sent on the implementation of the plan?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are regular reports on the implementation of the plan, as we said previously when we were talking about reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So who are these reports sent to on the implementation of the plan?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: These reports on the implementation of the plan are sent to the administrations in charge in Belgrade, the one for crime, the one for the crime police and then for the traffic police, and so on and so forth not to go into all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do these reports affect the general evaluation of the work of the secretariats of the interior and the employees employed therein?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the implementation of these plans. It is the entire secretariat and every individual employed in the secretariat that is assessed precisely on that basis according to the implementation of these plans, and that is what the performance evaluation depends on for individuals and secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your secretariat in Gnjilane, did it send plans -- reports on the implementation of their work-plans to the MUP staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Not in 1999, when I was chief, we did not send such reports to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to call up in e-court 6D269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you look at that, Mr. Gavranic, can you tell us your understanding of the purpose of the MUP staff for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I experienced the staff as an auxiliary organ that helped us, the secretariats, in our work in every way. When we needed assistance in any way, when we needed consultations to take place and things like that, especially in wartime. It was easier to get to Pristina, for couriers to get to Pristina rather than Belgrade. So my experience of it was it being an auxiliary body that helped us do our work at the SUPs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give an example of the assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for example, for instance, say material resources, material technical resources that were lacking, if we needed something like that, then we would send an urgent request through the staff so that this be submitted to the secretariats. So everything we asked for starting with these logistics or some technical equipment. I mean, after all when the staff would ask for this it would be easier for us to get it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me a specific example that actually happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for example, we need passports. We send a request for passports and we ask the staff if they have some in their reserves; and if they did have any reserves, then we would get this from the staff. If they had an instrument that had to do with crime investigations, we would get that in relation to an investigation regarding a particular case or crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What I'm finding difficult to understand at the moment is why there should be some body that's not a normal organizational unit established to provide extra passports or a crime investigation tool. These don't sound like bodies that -- things that need a body established for the fight against terrorism to be involved. Is that a -- is that the most important they did for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, and I was chief in Zrenjanin for many years before that, there always was a staff in Pristina. I mentioned a few ad hoc examples, just off the cuff, but the staff had an analysis person who had better insight into the overall situation with regard to all of these areas for which there are secretariats. The staff brought all of this together, this entire subject matter, and I believe that it helped a great deal thereby in terms of all the reports that were made at the level of public security. That was our experience of it, as an auxiliary body, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavranic, do you have before you document 6D269?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to this document, first of all, what's this all about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia dated the 18th of February, 1999, that was sent out to the organizational units of the public security section in headquarters; to the SUP, all 33 of them; the staff of the ministry in Pristina; the police stations, from 1 to 35; to the RDB; and it was sent by the assistant minister, head of the public security section, Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: SPP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Stations of the border police, because they are directly linked to appropriate administrations of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1999, did you work according to a plan that you had elaborated on the basis of the programme of the ministry for that year?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, we made this plan at the beginning of the year, and we started working on the basis of that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The SUP of Gnjilane, in February and March 1999, did it receive any dispatches from the minister and from the head of the public security section saying what the priority tasks were in the coming period?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: We did receive dispatches, I see that this was one of those dispatches, as far as I remember we got two or three dispatches, and priority tasks are set in these dispatches in accordance with the circumstances involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this dispatch have priority in relation to the plan that had been previously elaborated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This dispatch significantly changes the plans on the basis of which we were working. That is to say that this dispatch sets the priorities in our future work and this is the 18th of February, 1999, this is a time of great tensions because of the Rambouillet talks and the expected aggression. And I see that what is ordered here are measures that are based on a plan or that leave aside the plans on the basis of which we started working at the beginning of the year. As far as I can see here, the priority tasks of the SUPs are spelled out here as well as of the appropriate administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us move on now and look at paragraph 1. It says: "Update the defence plan, focusing on the plan of stand-by measures, mobilisation plan, and plan of organizations preparations for defence." And then it says further on: "Particularly update establishment lists of active and reserve policemen, recruit to full capacity, the 21st through 87th Detachments of the PJP," and so on. Tell us, what's the defence plan actually?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This defence plan is one that every SUP had. The officer for defence preparations within the police prepared that, so this person had precisely what is mentioned here. What is requested here is that at this point in time, in the month of February, this plan be activated, and according to the plan on stand-by measures, mobilisation plan, and plan for organizations preparations for defence. So the level of readiness of the SUP was supposed to be upgraded on the whole and mobilisation was supposed to be carried out and lists of reservists were supposed to be updated; and then also one had to see on the basis of this plan what facilities should be preserved in case of an aggression, is it the SUP building, police stations, and so on. So these plans were plans that all the SUPs had and they were elaborated by the officer that existed for these purposes in every SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now call up in e-court 6D238.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who sent this dispatch and when, tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch dated the 24th of March, 1999, it was sent by the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic. This is a dispatch that was sent precisely when the state of war was declared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's the distinction between this dispatch and the previous one dated the 18th of February, 1999, that was marked as 6D269?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, what I see here in the first paragraph is that the minister does invoke this dispatch of the 18th of February, 1999, and then he says even more specifically what the priority tasks of the SUP -- SUPs are. And then he says in even more specific terms what the priority task is in the further work of the secretariats of the interior at that point in time, because after all it is the 24th of March, 1999, that is to say that the aggression had already been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please call up in e-court document 6D132.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who sent this dispatch, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic on the 25th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's the difference now between this dispatch and the previous two that were marked as 6D269 and 6D238?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, dispatch -- this dispatch in paragraph 1 invokes the two previous ones, but it spells out even more specifically what the priorities and priority tasks of the secretariats of the interior are. I am trying to find it here, the minister instructing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, mobilise reservists and so on and so forth. So it spells out our priority tasks in even more specific terms. The bombing had already started, it was already in full sway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what was the point of these dispatches, all three dispatches, in relation to the annual plan of the SUP of Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The essence of all three dispatches is in the following: They completely leave aside the plan that we had had. According to that plan, we continued doing police work but these were our priorities, this set the priorities, and everything else was done only once all of these priorities were taken care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you look at this dispatch or a similar one, did you ever receive something like that in Kosovo and Metohija from the staff -- the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, we never received any such dispatch from the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let us move on to disciplinary responsibility, and I am going to ask you the following: Is disciplinary responsibility envisaged and prescribed for members of the police?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, disciplinary responsibility is prescribed for the members of the police on the basis of the Law on the Interior, and I think that it is also based on a decree and on the rule book for -- of conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P1737 is the relevant exhibit; the decree and disciplinary responsibility in the MUP is P1016; and the rule book on the internal organization of the MUP is 3, or rather, 6D1305. I'm not going to use these documents for the time being, but I'm going to ask you what kind of violations can there be of work duty?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: There can be light infractions and more serious ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to focus on this. You were chief before the bombing started and -- I mean chief in Zrenjanin. From the 1st of January, 1999, you became the chief in Gnjilane and you stayed there until after the bombing started, you stayed in Gnjilane. So let us subdivide this into two periods. Up until the beginning of April when a bylaw was passed and a period before that. So now I'm going to ask you the following: Before the beginning of the war, who takes measure in terms of light infractions and who does it in the case of serious infractions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: At the level of the Gnjilane SUP for lighter infractions, measures are passed by the chief of the SUP; and in the second instance it would be the disciplinary court at the SUP level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the bombing began at a specific time were there any changes in this area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, sometime in early April a decree was published regulating these matters, and it was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to have Exhibit 6D133 on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Gnjilane SUP receive a dispatch on the disciplinary responsibility in time of war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And is this this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who sent the dispatch?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It was sent by the assistant of the relevant sector of the Ministry of Interior, Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the last page of this document on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise General Djordjevic's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we can go back to the first page, please. Can you please tell us who were the recipients of this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The dispatch was received by the secretariats of internal affairs, organizational units at the head office of the ministry, the college of internal affairs, secondary school of internal affairs, the disciplinary court, and the higher disciplinary court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija among the recipients?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, you can see that it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This dispatch, does it explain, among other things, the disciplinary responsibility topic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, this decree relates to the decree on wartime where disciplinary responsibilities also clarify. The decree explains how to pass measures relating disciplinary responsibility in these new conditions, and the sentences or punishments were increased and those who were deciding on the measures were changed. So there were different people now responsible for passing the sentences and there was a different organization.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph we see the decree on internal affairs during the state of war that was published on the 17th -- on the 7th of April, 1999, and the actual decree bears the date the 9th of April, 1999 -- dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the top third of the page there is a paragraph beginning chief of the public security sector. Can you please read that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: "The chief of the public security sector has authorised the leaders of the organizational units to pass decreed measures and punishments for more serious infringements of work, duties, and obligations," and this is being attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, specifically the chief of the SUP now said in this new decree, which is mentioned in the dispatch, that a punishment in the first degree for more serious violations, whereas before these more serious violations were dealt with by the higher disciplinary court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 6D1342, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What are you saying is the change here in relation to more serious offences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The change was only in who was passing these measures. Now, before the dispatch and this decree for more serious infringements the chief of SUP could not pass a punishment; it was the disciplinary court at the level of the SUP. In the second instance, because it's a two-step procedure, the higher court in Belgrade was responsible. With this dispatch, the chief of the SUP who at that time passed sentences for less-serious infringements was now authorised to pass measures for more serious infringements of work duties in the first instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see 6D1342 in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, the objection I raised earlier applies to this one, it also applies to the previous one for which we had late notification. But this one is compounded by the fact that I can't find the translation to this document. If we had had an earlier notification, if it is a shorter document, I might have been able to get a slight translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When should these have been notified?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My understanding of the rule is that they ought to have been notified on, at the latest, last Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you tell us what the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. During the testimony of Mr. Mijatovic actually this was raised, and I think it's stayed unclear after his testimony. So we -- only after he finished his testimony I was able to continue my work with this witness and try to clarify that field or area for Your Honours and for everybody in the courtroom too. But I understand the procedure, actually, disciplinary procedure inside MUP of Serbia. So the fact is that really we sent it -- I don't know, we sent two groups of documents, one on I think Saturday and one yesterday, and it -- it is the late notice, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a translation for this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We just checked. We don't have a translation for this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This one is only continuation of the previous one, so it just gives more specifics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what is it you intend to ask the witness about this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to establish the sending, to whom, and to read one paragraph, paragraph 2 on the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will allow you to continue with reference to this document, but it is unfortunate, Mr. Lukic, that this is happening. And if necessary, we will grant indulgence to Mr. Stamp to enable him to prepare adequately for cross-examination. Meanwhile, please continue with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that you don't like to talk about this topic in details, but I was just informed that all our documents are now rejected by the CLSS, except for the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's something I find it very difficult to accept as a bold statement, Mr. Lukic. There's no point in us debating it here, I don't know the circumstances, but you can rest assured I will make urgent inquiries into the circumstances and find out what the position is and I will deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Meanwhile proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, you have this document in front of you, 6D1342?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is send this document, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The document is being sent by the MUP of Serbia public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who signed it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It was signed by the assistant minister General-Major Petar Zekovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To whom is it being sent -- actually, let's cut it short. Let's not spend too much time on this. Is the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija among the recipients?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the second paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: "In the disciplinary proceedings for a serious infringement of work duties and obligations, the disciplinary report is being submitted by the direct manager, the chief of the department, the chief of the station, the chief of independent sector, and so on to the head of the basic organizational units (the chief of the headquarters at the seat the chief of the secretariat director or other)."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one clarification, please. We will continue. I think it is quite clear in the transcript after all. Who is authorised according to this dispatch for the -- these infringements? Is it the same instance as in the previous dispatch and can you just -- but it's explained in more detail?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same as in the previous dispatch but it's explained here in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at 6D885.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please look at that on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that on the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the 2nd of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which SUP is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: It's the SUP in Zrenjanin, the police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time who was the chief of the SUP in Zrenjanin?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I was the chief of the SUP in Zrenjanin at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what does this document deal with? Just tell us. You don't have to read it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This is a disciplinary infringement by a policeman from Zrenjanin committed at the time he was sent to Kosovo and Metohija on assignments with the PJP. The infringement was committed in Kosovo and Metohija and the disciplinary proceedings were conducted by us in the Zrenjanin SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: From what I can see here, it involved dismissal, and he did appeal to the higher disciplinary court which actually upheld the decision on dismissal from what I can see here. It was a serious violation of work duties, and the measure that was passed for this was dismissal from his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For a person to be employed at the Ministry of Internal Affairs, what sort of background check did have to be done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're now moving -- if you're moving away, I would like to understand this in simple language. What was the change made in the disciplinary procedure in -- at the beginning of the April 1999? Just tell us in simple language what changed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's like this. Everything stayed the same as far as violations of work duty is concerned, but the disciplinary courts, or rather, those organs that were passing the sentences were different. So broader authorisation or authority was given to the chief of the SUP as of April. The disciplinary courts were always two steps -- I apologise to the interpreters. For lighter violations of work duties there is a dual procedure. At the level of the secretariat the sentence at the first instance is passed by the chief of SUP. If the worker appeals, then he's sent to the disciplinary court that exists in the SUP. If it's a more serious infringement then the disciplinary procedure at the first instance is conducted by the disciplinary court at the level of the secretariat. And then the higher disciplinary court kicks in if the worker appeals, and that's at the level of the SUP in Belgrade. This decree then changed the situation. Now, the chief of the SUP was authorised, so he no longer passed measures for light violations but in the first instance for serious violations of work duties and obligations. So his authority has been broadened and the sentences were stricter. Excuse me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who was the appeal to then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
