utterances.text: [Interpretation] The disciplinary prosecutor or the actual employee could submit the appeal. The worker could always engage a defence attorney, at any step he could do that. I mean, I didn't really go into that much, but they could all lodge an appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were there still two levels of appeal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, who were the people on these disciplinary courts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The disciplinary court comprised - and you can see that from the dispatches - of people who worked at the Ministry of Internal Affairs. So at the level of the ministry the higher disciplinary court included -- I saw generals and at the SUP level in Gnjilane or Zrenjanin we formed a disciplinary court comprising the employees at the Gnjilane or the Zrenjanin SUP. We would make up a trial panel, a panel of judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it follow from what you've said, Mr. Gavranic, that at the less-serious level the members of the disciplinary court were your inferior officers, your subordinate officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If we are talking about the month of April and the decree, members of the disciplinary court within the SUP were the second-degree body in charge of lighter violations of duties in service. I was the disciplinary organ for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I understand that. The point I'm making to you I want to be clear about is, in their ordinary, everyday jobs, the people who made up the lower disciplinary court were actually subordinate officers of yours in the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean in the hierarchy, when they are doing their regular jobs? In terms of hierarchy, when they are not members of the disciplinary court they are subordinate to me; when they are sitting in a panel, they are not, they are independent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, some of us would find that difficult to understand. Anyway, please -- I've now understood the set-up which seems rather strange, but please continue, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These disciplinary courts have nothing to do with criminal liability, do they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No. Criminal liability is decided by regular courts. This is disciplinary liability.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can two proceedings, disciplinary and criminal, be parallel?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, and they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something about finding employment with the ministry. In order for a person to be admitted on a job at the ministry, what kind of vetting did they have to go through?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: To be accepted in a vacancy at the ministry, they had to undergo vetting that was much stricter than anywhere else in the republic. Medical examination in specialised institutions, information was asked from the judiciary and courts, vetting was also done by the police covering their territory concerning personal information. So the requirements to be met before one is employed with the ministry were much higher than elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of units did this apply to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: All employees of the MUP, all employees of the MUP had to be vetted in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard how you came to become the chief of SUP Gnjilane. What did your predecessor inform you about as he was handing over his duties to you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Before me this post was occupied by Colonel Vladica Milosavljevic, who was going to retire. During hand-over, take-over, of duties he informed me about the state of affairs in various areas, various fields of activity for which the SUP was in charge. What was important to me was that there were no terrorist actions in 1998 when he was chief; and therefore there were no anti-terrorist actions. No units were sent to Gnjilane from Serbia proper and there were no detachments active in the area of SUP Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did the KLA appear in your territory, if they appeared?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: According to my information, it was in the beginning of 1990 [as interpreted] that the KLA made a more serious appearance, namely, in Kosovska Kamenica. More precisely, from the information I received from the state security sector, there was an operative zone established called Karadak, an operative zone of the KLA involving two brigades, 171 and 172 Brigades of the KLA, but they were passive to begin with in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire, the record at page 93, line 5, the date or the year is correct. I thought I heard something else in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavranic, let's clear up one thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did the KLA appear in the territory of your SUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Beginning 1999, beginning 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know which brigades of the KLA began to act there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I already said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I was looking for that error in the transcript, and I missed your answer; you've given it. Was it in Gnjilane that the regional centre of the OSCE was set up?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes. The regional centre of the OSCE headed by Richard Heaslip with the deputy Mr. Crnjakov was set up, and there were coordination centres in Gnjilane, Kosovska Kamenica, and Vitina; and they had offices [Realtime transcript read in error "officers"] in three villages, one purely Albanian, one purely Serbian, and one mixed. The Albanian village was Pozaranje, Raniluk was a purely Serbian village, and Zitinja was a mixed village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any problems with their activities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: As for cooperation with the OSCE, I think it was very fair, very correct. We met every Monday to exchange any information we had about incidents, although their activity was sometimes inconsistent with the mandate, their mandate, as we were informed of it. They were frequently in the border belt on the Macedonian border, and this cooperation we had had to do with reporting crimes and cross-checking information because it often happened that ethnic Albanians were reluctant to report a crime to us, and then an OSCE officer in charge of crime investigation would come; and we would cross-check our information, and we would realize that some -- we had missed something and then we would go on site to perform an on-site investigation if we had been advised of the incident by the OSCE officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the transcript reflects that OSCE had officers in three villages, was it officers or offices?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think offices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, let's move to another subject. Could you tell us something about inter-ethnic relations in the area of your secretariat in early 1999?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: In the first months of 1999 there was already noticeable tension in the territory of our secretariat, as in the whole Kosovo and Metohija, but there were no major disruptions between ethnic communities nor were there any major crimes perpetrated at that time there were no killings, rapes, and aggravated robberies. All I can remember is one terrorist action against the clinic of Dr. Sadiku, a bomb was thrown from a car and we filed a criminal report against an unidentified perpetrator. There was tension, it could be felt, but there were not -- the incidence of crime was not high.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who was the injured party by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: An Albanian, Dr. Sadiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did OSCE representatives inform you they had to leave your area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, if it was an important matter. On the 19th in the evening they requested a meeting, I mean the 19th of March, and they asked SUP Gnjilane to provide them with safe passage as they leave. We agreed that the next morning the patrols that would secure their evacuation should do their job, and early in the morning on the 20th of March they left the area of SUP Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The events continued to develop as they did, but do you remember when the state of immediate threat of war was proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: That was on the 23rd and 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened after?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The air-strikes began. The first bomb fell in Silovo village, and that's why I remember it. It fell on the house of the chief of the duty service, his entire family was there. It happened at 8.05 on the 24th and then the air-strikes began on the whole Gnjilane and environs. Chaos and panic reigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it then that some units were deployed in your area and whose units?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, when the state of immediate threat of war and the state of war were proclaimed, VJ units were deployed across the area of the SUP of Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you list some installations and targets that were hit in the first days of the war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The barracks that was in the town of Gnjilane itself was bombed relentlessly, but also some industrial complexes, construction businesses, motorists' societies, businesses that were essential to the economic life.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there bombing outside the town of Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that the Army of Yugoslavia took up position mainly outside population centres, so the positions of the VJ were bombed but bombs also fell on population centres and that's why a large number of residents started to flee in the first days of the war. That was what the situation was like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, the bomb that fell on the house that you say of the chief of the duty service and his family, were they killed by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fortunately, no. The bomb passed through the entire house and exploded in the back yard. His wife and daughters were inside the house, and it was very fortunate that no one was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell what the target was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. That's a village several kilometres away from Gnjilane, 2 or 3 kilometres away from the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now call up in e-court 6D209.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have this document, 209. 6D209 you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's a map of Gnjilane. We have it on the screen now. Could the usher please help you, give you a pen. Now I'm going to ask you the following question: In your territory were there any established MUP check-points when the bombing began.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: When the bombing began, there were only at the very beginning a few MUP check-points. But we were afraid that these check-points would become a target for NATO bombs, so we oriented ourselves towards patrol activities. However, for a short period of time they were there and from time to time they were re-established but in a very discreet way, very discreet way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on the map, or rather, can you see this on the map, can you see -- just a moment, please. Could you stop at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have this map moved up or is it -- sorry, sorry, that's fine. I see something completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavranic, could you please mark these police check-points for us at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war they were in the village of Klokot, near the village of Klokot on the road, between Gnjilane-Urosevac. That is one of the main roads. Then the road between Gnjilane and Vranje, Kmetovci, so on the roads. It is mostly roads that were under police control.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 1 next to your first dot and number 2 next to your second dot.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any others?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, there were but not check-points in a classical sense. These were patrols that would stop there and control the movement of goods and vehicles, but very discreetly because of this great fear of the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a different-coloured pen now or could the usher help you and give you a different-coloured pen.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to change the colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I ask for assistance, please, different colour. It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, you've changed it seems. So now can I ask you the following: Were there any check-points of the Army of Yugoslavia in your territory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were check-points of the Army of Yugoslavia too, towards --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: They were very close to us, not in the village of Klokot but right before the village of Klokot. It seems on the map here that Klokot is on this main road, but it's not. It's further in-depth along the road to Vitina and in Kmetovci, they also had a check-point, but again it is a bit more on the side, that is where the check-point of the Army of Yugoslavia is, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, it's very nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And could you place numbers 3 and 4 there, Klokot 3 and the other one can be number 4.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Later on were joint check-points established?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, joint check-points were established later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be given an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC188, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please call up in e-court P1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have it in front of you, Mr. Gavranic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. What was it 19 ...

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is minutes of a meeting with senior police officials in Kosovo and Metohija dated the 4th of April, 1999. Did you see this document during proofing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see whether you attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I did attend in meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2 now, and I'd like to draw your attention to paragraph 4. In paragraph 4 can you find your own name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it was that you reported about at that meeting, you and your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This was a meeting at the MUP staff on the 4th of April, so this was a collegium meeting of the MUP in Pristina. We reported about the state of security in the respective territories of our SUPs. Since it was the 4th of April and since that was the first part of the bombing when indeed there was fear, panic, many crimes were committed because passions were aflame, and there was a lot of robbery, theft, killings; and we spoke of what the situation was like at that point in time, and we talked about the measures taken against the perpetrators. What the situation was in respect of the population, that it started leaving the territory of the secretariat, what the situation was regarding terrorists in the territory of the secretariat, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In which direction were people mainly going from your area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: At first, during those first few days of the bombing, for the most part they went towards Serbia, women, children, irrespective of ethnic background, women, children, old men, they all set off to Vranje first and foremost. Some went to their relatives where they felt it was safe, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see a reference to Vranje here as well, is Vranje in Kosovo or --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No, no, Vranje it is in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had information that some inhabitants were coming back to the territory of your SUP from Vranje?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were making some estimates at that point in time as to how many people were moving out, how many people were going, how many people were coming back, because it was the task of the police to encourage them to stay on and to guarantee their safety and security, not to leave the area, that everything would be fine in no time, and many people did indeed come back. They would relocate their families but they would come back. Because of the situation that prevailed, indeed there were a lot of civilians, a lot of people on the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You as the SUP, did you regularly report on these occurrences?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the information that we discussed earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did civilians start leaving the village of Zegra and who were they and why were they leaving?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Already during the first few days of the war the biggest migration of civilians took place in the territory of the town of Gnjilane itself and in the territory of the village of Zegra and the surrounding villages. First of all, the Mucibaba mountain pass is up there and that was taken up like the mountains towards Macedonia by the Army of Yugoslavia and that was bombed the most. Those were the positions of the Army of Yugoslavia that were bombed the most during those first few days, so there was fear of bombing then there were multiple murders in the village of Zegra. So the first refugees from the village of Zegra were actually Serbs who arrived in Gnjilane because this was a mixed ethnic village, the majority population was Albanian, and the Serb families moved out as they feared revenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D614 called up in e-court, page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who's who in all of this is very difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will clarify all those killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Please continue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the bottom of page 814.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is 814 about, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Gnjilane on the 28th of March, 1999, aggravated theft under Article 166; that's what I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page now, please, page 320, and would you look at 815 through 821.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are numerous crimes that were committed on the 28th of March, aggravated theft and also there were cases of murder and arson.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the persons mentioned here, were criminal reports filed against them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like page 36 of this same exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just don't move just for a moment, please. These are all aggravated theft unless -- there's one that we can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those are all aggravated thefts. You're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness said they included murder and arson --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're coming to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're coming that. Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So now we need page 36, please, paragraph 85.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was reported in paragraph 85?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of March, 1999, causing public danger under Article 187 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Serbia, it is the crime of arson, the injured party was unknown, and the perpetrators who were arrested, Radancic Bojan, Petkovic Nenad, Marinkovic Sveta, Vuckovic Svetomir, Denic Goran, and Radancic Dejan, all of them civilians. The perpetrators were remanded in custody pursuant to Article 196 of the law on criminal procedure. A criminal complaint was filed against the identified perpetrators, and it was forwarded to the office of the municipal public prosecutor in Gnjilane on the 3rd of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the ethnicity of these persons who were arrested because of theft at the end of March, and what is the ethnicity of these people here who were charged with having committed the crime of arson?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Well, different ethnic backgrounds. There are Albanians and Serbs, more Serbs as far as I can see here from these documents; but there are people of different ethnic backgrounds involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to deal with some other crimes and then we're going to deal with the most serious ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we identify one committed by an Albanian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For that we need page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I mean among the ones we've seen so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need page 320. [Interpretation] We can see some here, also just a moment, please. We've already reached 320.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you see point 816?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 28th of March, 1999, aggravated theft, Kajtazi Nehat was the perpetrator a civilian from Vitina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's his ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let us go back to page 36. We need number 87.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of a crime is this, who is the injured party, and who is the murderer?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of April, 1999, the offence of murder was committed to the detriment of Morina Nazim. Morina Ejup, a civilian of the village of Odanovce, committed the offence. He was placed in detention pursuant to Article 196 of the law on criminal procedure, and a criminal complaint was filed and forwarded to the office of the district public prosecutor in Gnjilane on the 7th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you tell us what the injured party and the accused person by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Both were Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show page 9, please, so that we can discuss different kinds of crimes. We need number 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which crime was committed by whom against whom?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Kosovska Kamenica, 30th April, 1999, acts of indecency under Article 108 of the Criminal Code of Serbia. The perpetrator was Momcilo Jovanovic, a member of the reserve police force of the SUP in Gnjilane, committed an act of indecency against Ismalji Emrije.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who were the perpetrator and injured party by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Perpetrator Serbian, injured party Albanian woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was done?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The perpetrator was -- had a criminal report filed against him and was turned over to the criminal court in Gnjilane, he was remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to slow down a little. We have to turn to page 146, items 87 and 88.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do we have page 146?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Items 87 and 88, can you tell us -- 86 --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: 87, Kosovska Kamenica --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you take 86 first -- no, 87, that's your area.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: 87 is Kosovska Kamenica, 7th May 1999, aggravated theft was committed, as defined by Article 166 of the Criminal Code of Serbia. The perpetrator was Sasa Arsic, member of the reserve police from the Gnjilane SUP. He was a resident of the village of Berivojce in Kosovska Kamenica municipality. He was remanded in custody under Article 196 of the Law on Criminal Procedure. The injured party was not identified. A criminal complaint KU 48/99 was filed against the perpetrator and submitted to the municipal public prosecutor's office in Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And item 88, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Gnjilane, 7th May 1999, again allege elevated theft under the aim article, 166 of the Criminal Code of Serbia. Perpetrator was Cvetko Petrovic, member of the reserve police with the Gnjilane SUP. He was a resident of Bodrige village in Gnjilane municipality. He was remanded in custody under Article 196. The injured party was not identified. A criminal report was filed and submitted to the municipal public prosecutor's office in Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 147, please, item 94. Can we see what this is about? It's end May 1999.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The crime is aggravated theft on 26th May 1999. The injured party was Destan Mehmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Albanian. This crime was elucidated. The perpetrator was Akagijan Dzemeilji from Gnjilane, again Albanian, member of the reserve police force. He was remanded in custody and a criminal report was filed with the municipal public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can't see it on the screen yet, page 350. As far as I can see, all these items are related to your area. What crimes are concerned in all these items?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: All of them are aggravated theft, Article 166 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was a criminal report filed in each of these cases?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the ethnicity of all the accused here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Serbs, civilians, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to the criminal offences, but to follow the chronology we heard that air-strikes began. Do you know when it began and do you know when the SUP in Pristina building was hit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, the night of the 28th March.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you leave the building of SUP Gnjilane, if you left?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: After the building of SUP Gnjilane [as interpreted] was destroyed, all secretariats following a dispatch had to move and find another location from which to work. Thus, the SUP in Gnjilane and the department of internal affairs in Kosovska Kamenica and Vitina and the police station in Novo Brdo, we all had to move to back-up locations that we frequently changed throughout the war. Because the secretariats, the SUPs, were regular targets during air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in line 23 there, was that a reference to the building of the SUP in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which SUP building was destroyed on the night of the 28th March?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: The building of SUP Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We speak too fast, both of us, and it's normal that this results in mistakes. After you relocated from that building of SUP Gnjilane, did the duty service continue to operate?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: No. The jobs -- the functions of the duty service were quite different in this situation, and in fact it ceased to operate because the basic preconditions for its work no longer existed in Kosovska Kamenica, Vitina, or in the police station in Novo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up in e-court 6D335.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have this exhibit in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid we have no translation for this. I'll just ask you what was this case about?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I cease to object sometimes with these documents because the witness is here, and he might as well speak about them while he's here. But if the documents are untranslated could I request through the Court that at least evidence is led as to the authenticity of the document, what it is, before they go into the terms of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you deal with that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 2 we see an official note. Could you tell us where it was written, by whom?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: This is an official note written on the 19th of July, 2001, on the premises of SUP Gnjilane in Vranje related to an attempted murder, as stipulated by Article 47/19 against Skender Seljimi from Zegra village, Gnjilane municipality. On the 30th of March, 1999, at 1400 hours Skender Seljimi from Zegra village, Gnjilane municipality reported to the duty service that two members of the VJ perpetrated the crime of attempted murder and robbery defined by appropriate articles of the Criminal Code in his house. Upon receiving this report, members of the crime police department of SUP Gnjilane brought into the SUP Stojan Markovic from Grdelice and Dejan Jankovic from Leskovac, VJ members both. They were remanded in custody under Article 196 on the Law on Criminal Procedure, and on the 31st of March, 1999, a criminal report was filed against them to the municipality prosecutor's office in Pristina Number KU 182/99, follows the criminal report and all the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The injured party was what ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Ethnic Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what was done after this, what was done with this -- with these accused?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: I remember the -- this incident in Zegra because it was typical for the beginning of the war and that whole period in the area of SUP Gnjilane. I think this charge was later changed, it was re-qualified because the injured party died and court proceedings are not within the jurisdiction of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if this person was turned over to military authorities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you enjoy the support of the VJ prosecuting this and similar cases?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: In this initial period because of great problems in Zegra village, we did have the support of VJ members, but the arrest was done by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bear with me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to find a document that has been translated. I'd like to call 6D69 in e-court. This is a case that's rather large, I mean the file is rather large, 70 pages; so we won't go through them. But you say that this case around Zegra is familiar to you. So tell us if you can what happened the next day after that described incident, what happened in the village?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: In those last days of March, the 29th, 30th, 31st March, multiple killings took place in the village of Zegra. After the first reports came in about three murders, I believe it was at first, an on-site investigation team went out, the investigation judge was informed and we in SUP Gnjilane formed an operative group headed by the chief of crime police. The job of that group was to deal with this and similar incidents in the period that follows. We had knowledge that the perpetrators were members of the Army of Yugoslavia. The investigating judge went out onto the scene and performed an on-site investigation. The next day we received another report of a multiple murder in the area of Zegra village. Our response was the same. We formed an on-site investigation team and informed the investigating judge, and according to our information, or rather, based on our information, we made some arrests. We arrested a rather large group of members of the Army of Yugoslavia, including Vlado Zmajevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think you have some names on the screen in this document.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: May I continue? Zmajevic -- Vlado Smajovic and others. These arrests were very hard. I was helped by the garrison commander and the arrests were made by the policemen of SUP Gnjilane. I'm saying it was very hard because it was the initial chaos of war when everybody was armed, everybody was dangerous, and we knew that if we don't react appropriately to this first wave the existence of our SUP would become pointless in the area we were covering.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We still have little time before the break. Explain how the arrest was made?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Upon learning of this crime, since it concerned members of the VJ, I informed the superior whom I was able to locate at the moment and that was garrison commander Ranko Milinovic. He asked me because he didn't have the strength, and it was right at the beginning, those first few days when military courts were still not operating. So I took a few reinforced patrols of the police. I went to the site and in the usual police way, we managed to bring in a large number of persons and identify the perpetrators. We immediately remanded six VJ members in custody. We informed the investigating judge and the prosecutor, and we informed the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's -- we just need a reference for the record regarding this case in Zegra, it's 6D1127 and 6D810, but we're not going to open them now. Could we now call up in e-court 6D333. Since we don't have the translation, I'd like to ask you: Do you remember the murder of Fitim Isufi in Zegra village?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you in relation to all these incidents, in addition to the particularly difficult conditions, that is, despite the particularly difficult conditions, did the police go out to investigate on site?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC
utterances.text: Yes, even at the beginning of the war when the conditions were impossible we tried to react to every report, regardless of who it was about and whose jurisdiction it officially was. And I remember the person you are mentioning now, it was a retarded person and we received a report that his body was found somewhere in the first week of April in Zegra village. Sometimes we had to wait for a couple of days before going out to investigate because it was not safe to go into certain areas. It was a mountainous area, and the lowest point was 500 metres above sea level. Other areas were between 700 and 1200 metres above sea level. It was a heavily wooded mountainous area, were dangerous for police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, I think that's all we can manage today. We'll continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Gavranic, we have to conclude our proceedings for today at this stage, and we shall resume tomorrow. That means you have to return, I'm afraid, tomorrow to continue your evidence and hopefully complete it, that will be at 9.00 tomorrow morning in this courtroom. Meanwhile, I have to draw your attention to an important rule that we have, that you must have no communication with anyone at all about the evidence in the case between now and continuing your evidence tomorrow; and that applies to any evidence in this case whether it's evidence we've heard or evidence that may yet be heard. You can talk about anything else but absolutely no communication whatsoever with anyone about the evidence. Now could you please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we shall see you again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.33 p.m.,
